title: Google Pixel 11 Faces $100 Price Hike as RAM Strategy Shifts Across Lineup
excerpt: Leaked Amazon listings reveal Google is dropping 128GB storage entirely and introducing tiered RAM configurations, with the base Pixel 11 starting at $899 ahead of an August 12 unveiling.
body:
• The entire Pixel 11 lineup will cost roughly $100 more than its predecessors, with the base model starting at $899 and the Pro Fold reaching $2,249 for the 1TB variant.
  • Google is eliminating 128GB storage across the board, making 256GB the new entry point — a move that partially offsets the price increase.
  • The Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL will ship with 12GB of RAM at the 256GB tier, down from the universal 16GB on last year's Pro models, reflecting the ongoing global memory shortage.
  • Google has been investing in Android-level memory optimization, with Android 17 introducing RAM-based app memory limits and new developer tools to reduce app footprints.

Google's next flagship smartphone lineup is shaping up to be its most expensive yet. Accidentally published Amazon listings — since removed — have revealed US pricing, storage configurations, and specifications for the Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL, and Pixel 11 Pro Fold, painting a picture of across-the-board price increases coupled with a strategic shift in RAM allocation.

The listings, first surfaced by Droid Life and corroborated by Android Authority reader screenshots, show the base Pixel 11 priced at $899 for 256GB of storage — $100 more than the Pixel 10's $799 starting price. The Pixel 11 Pro jumps to $1,099, the Pro XL to $1,299, and the Pro Fold to $1,899. Each represents a flat $100 increase over its predecessor.

The Storage Swap

Google is discontinuing the 128GB base storage tier entirely. Every Pixel 11 model will start at 256GB, with 512GB and 1TB options available on Pro models. While this means buyers get double the entry-level storage compared to last year, the practical effect is still a higher minimum price of entry.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=exy9Jyt47vQ

The approach mirrors what Apple did recently with the Mac mini lineup — removing a lower-priced configuration rather than raising the sticker price on an existing one. For Google, it simplifies manufacturing and retail while letting the company frame the increase as a storage upgrade rather than a straightforward hike.

"It may 'just' be a $100 price bump, but it removes any value edge this year's Pixels could have had against the competition."

— Joe Maring, Android Authority

RAM Takes a Step Back on Pro Models

The more notable change is what is happening with RAM. According to the leaked Amazon listings, the 256GB variants of the Pixel 11 Pro and Pro XL will ship with 12GB of RAM. Only the 512GB and 1TB configurations retain 16GB. The standard Pixel 11 is listed at 12GB across both storage tiers, while the Pro Fold maintains 16GB at every level.

This marks a departure from the Pixel 10 Pro lineup, where Google offered 16GB of RAM universally — a specification the company had standardized starting with the Pixel 9 Pro series. The reduction comes against the backdrop of a global DRAM shortage, often dubbed "RAMageddon" within the industry, that has driven memory prices sharply higher. Samsung, Apple, and others have faced similar component cost pressures, with Samsung already raising prices on its Galaxy S26 series earlier this year.

Google's Software Response

Even as hardware RAM allocations shrink on some models, Google has been building out software-level countermeasures. At Google I/O 2026, the company announced that Android 17 will introduce conservative, device RAM-based app memory limits designed to prevent poorly optimized apps from destabilizing the system. The new limits target extreme memory leaks and outlier apps before they trigger system-wide instability.

Alongside these limits, Google unveiled the R8 Configuration Analyzer in Android Studio — a tool that helps developers identify and strip unnecessary code to reduce their app's memory footprint. The company cited banking app Monzo, which achieved a 30% improvement in cold starts and a 35% reduction in application-not-responding errors after optimizing its R8 configuration.

Separately, Google's Android Runtime (ART) team has shipped updates that reduce code size by an estimated 50 to 100 megabytes per device, reaching over one billion Android devices globally through mainline updates — no full OS upgrade required.

At I/O Connect Berlin in July 2026, Google engineers presented a dedicated session on optimizing app performance for the "next generation of Android," explicitly framing memory management as moving toward "enforced efficiency" across the ecosystem.

Competitive Pressure Mounts

At $899, the Pixel 11 would match the Samsung Galaxy S26's price and cost $100 more than the iPhone 17. The $1,099 Pixel 11 Pro lands at the same price as the iPhone 17 Pro, while the $1,299 Pro XL enters Galaxy S26 Ultra territory. For a brand that once positioned itself as the affordable flagship alternative, the shift is significant.

Google's own product lineup adds further complexity. The Pixel 10 Pro, currently available for as low as $699 during clearance sales at the Google Store, delivers roughly 90% of the Pixel 11 Pro experience at a fraction of the cost. The $499 Pixel 10a, meanwhile, offers seven years of software updates and Google's full AI feature set, making the $400 gap to the base Pixel 11 a tough sell for value-conscious buyers.

What to Expect on August 12

Google has confirmed that its Made by Google event will take place in New York on August 12, with Pixel 11 pre-orders expected to open the same day. Retail availability is pegged to August 20, according to earlier reports from French deal-tracking site Dealabs.

Beyond pricing, the Pixel 11 series is expected to feature Google's Tensor G6 chip, a new "Pixel Glow" RGB LED notification system around the camera bar, and incremental camera improvements. The rear-facing temperature sensor present on the Pixel 10 Pro models is being retired.

For consumers weighing their options, the calculation is straightforward but uncomfortable: pay more for modest hardware gains and less RAM in some configurations, or wait for the inevitable discounts that follow every Pixel launch. In a year when flagship phones are universally getting more expensive, Google is betting that its AI-first software story and ecosystem advantages will justify the premium — even as it quietly hands a stronger value argument to its own Pixel 10 lineup sitting on clearance shelves.
